title: Declared interests named in documents filed about a planning project
question: Do separate Board documents name a voting or recused member’s declared interest on the same page as the Planning case number?
finding: 5,300 searchable Board attachments were checked. 2,458 pages identified a single application tied to a dated roll call and a member disclosure. 4 of those pages also named a declared entity.
how: Join the exact Planning application number in the commission roll call to a page in a separately filed document. Compare the organization name there with that member’s recorded disclosure for the meeting year or either adjacent year. Each row links the minutes and the original attachment.
limits: A shared page can mention a neighbor, historical party or unrelated business. Each match requires the project role, the reporting period and the applicable conflict rules. Multiple applications on one page and filings outside this attachment collection need separate review.

rows.review: The bank is printed on the law firm’s check for the appeal fee. This page does not identify a project owner, designer or lender.
The packet describes a former bank tenant in the vacant building.
The packet says the bank and another former tenant had been vacant since 2019.
The area plan uses the bank’s name to identify the redevelopment site.
